data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.question: abruptly
sections.summary: Suddenly and unexpectedly, often in a way that seems rude or unplanned.

senses.definition: in a sudden and unexpected way, often seeming rude or without warning
examples: The meeting ended abruptly when the fire alarm went off.

answers.answer: He stopped talking abruptly.
He stopped abruptly to talk.
He was abrupt to stop talking.
He stopped talking in abruptly.

sections.question: absolutely
sections.summary: Completely and in every way; used to make a statement stronger.

senses.definition: completely and in every way; used for emphasis to make a statement stronger
examples: She was absolutely right about the decision.

answers.answer: I absolutely agree with you.
I agree absolutely with you.
I am absolute agree with you.
I absolutely agree to you.

sections.question: barely
sections.summary: Only just; almost not; by a very small amount.

senses.definition: only just; almost not; by a very small amount or to a very small degree
examples: She barely had enough time to catch the train.

answers.answer: I could barely hear the speaker.
I could hear barely the speaker.
I was barely to hear the speaker.
I could barely hear about the speaker.

sections.question: certainly
sections.summary: Without any doubt; definitely; used to show complete confidence.

senses.definition: without any doubt; used to emphasise that something is definitely true or will definitely happen
examples: He will certainly be at the meeting tomorrow.

answers.answer: I will certainly call you later.
I will call certainly you later.
I am certain call you later.
I will certainly call to you later.

sections.question: comparatively
sections.summary: To a certain degree when judged against something else; relatively.

senses.definition: to a certain degree when compared to something else or to a general standard; relatively
examples: The winters here are comparatively mild.

answers.answer: This exam was comparatively easy.
This exam was comparative easy.
Comparatively, it was easy than the last one.
This exam was comparatively to easy.

sections.question: completely
sections.summary: Totally and in every way; with nothing missing or left out.

senses.definition: in every way or as much as possible; totally and without leaving anything out
examples: I completely forgot about the appointment.

answers.answer: I completely forgot his name.
I forgot completely his name.
I complete forgot his name.
I completely forgot about to his name.

sections.question: definitely
sections.summary: Without any doubt; in a way that is certain and clear.

senses.definition: without any doubt; in a way that is certain and clear; used to emphasise a strong opinion or decision
examples: She will definitely come to the party.

answers.answer: I will definitely attend the meeting.
I will attend definitely the meeting.
I am definite attend the meeting.
I will definitely attend to the meeting.

sections.question: entirely
sections.summary: Completely and in every part; with nothing left out or excluded.

senses.definition: completely and in every part; with nothing left out or excluded
examples: The decision was entirely up to her.

answers.answer: I entirely understand your point.
I understand entirely your point.
I am entire understand your point.
I entirely understand about your point.

sections.question: extremely
sections.summary: To a very great degree; used to make an adjective or adverb much stronger.

senses.definition: to a very great degree; used to make an adjective or another adverb much stronger
examples: The journey was extremely long and tiring.

answers.answer: The test was extremely difficult.
The test was extreme difficult.
The test was extremely difficulty.
The test was extremely of difficult.

sections.question: fairly
sections.summary: To a moderate degree; more than a little but not very or extremely.

senses.definition: to a moderate degree; more than a little but less than very or extremely
examples: The hotel was fairly comfortable and well located.

answers.answer: The lesson was fairly easy to follow.
The lesson was fair easy to follow.
The lesson was fairly easiness to follow.
The lesson was fairly easy for follow.
